narrative.overview:
This is the second correction of this app's visual direction. The first rewrite mistakenly adopted estudio's own visual language. That was wrong: estudio keeps its own system; 1000m and gym-tracker are the pair that share one, and the shared one is gym-tracker's — Bebas Neue, SF Mono, a static tri-color mesh background, a single fixed app header, and the floating pill bottom-nav with its spring-eased sliding indicator. Three pieces of the retired estudio-style skin were kept anyway because they had genuinely earned their place: the Físico screen's card layout, the Historial list's flat row-with-left-dot-and-chevron, and red as the color of the Ajustes 'Eliminar' action.

The material is near-black frosted glass everywhere: translucent white-on-black cards over a slow-drifting three-color radial mesh (blue/lime/orange), with a near-invisible dot-grain texture on top. Big numbers are the loudest thing on screen in oversized Bebas Neue; everything administrative drops into small SF Mono. There is exactly one fixed header per screen and it never scrolls or duplicates.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black glass cards sharing one recipe: bg-card fill, hairline border, shadow-card
Bebas Neue oversized numerals for hero/stat/PR values; SF Mono for every logged or computed data point
A single fixed app-header per screen (never sticky, never duplicated) plus the floating pill bottom-nav with a spring-eased sliding indicator
Selected/active states invert to solid white-on-black, never a tinted accent
Static tri-color mesh background — no per-tab recoloring, no halo mechanic

rules.name: The One-Header Rule
rules.body: Exactly one .app-header exists per screen render, position:fixed, solid var(--bg) fill. Any title living inside scrolling content is never fixed or sticky — it scrolls normally.

rules.name: The Type-Owns-Its-Color Rule
rules.body: Each session type (series/rodaje/velocidad/test) keeps one fixed accent everywhere it appears — colors never migrate to generic chrome, and there is no per-tab background recoloring.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any value the user logged or the app computed from logged data renders in SF Mono; Bebas Neue is reserved for headline-scale numbers and short uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Equal-Grid Rule
rules.body: Every Planificación day block's field row is grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr) regardless of how many fields that day type needs — rodaje leaves 2 cells empty rather than using a narrower grid, so columns stay aligned across Lunes/Miércoles/Viernes.

dos: Do keep exactly one fixed app-header per screen; any other title scrolls with its content.
Do keep each session type's color fixed everywhere it appears — never per-tab background recoloring.
Do render every logged/derived value in SF Mono.
Do give every Planificación day block the same 4-column grid regardless of how many fields it uses.
Do treat the nav-indicator's colored glow and the today-hero's shine sweep as intentional gym-tracker brand commitments, not defects to flatten.
donts: Don't reintroduce Archivo/Archivo Narrow, a shifting background halo, or any other piece of the retired estudio-style skin.
Don't move Planificación back into Ajustes; it is its own apartado alongside Historial under the second tab.
Don't give a day block with fewer fields a narrower or re-centered grid — empty placeholder cells keep columns aligned.
Don't convert the Historial row or the Físico card layout back to gym-tracker's own native patterns — those two pieces are deliberate, named exceptions kept from the retired build.
